study type: Mixed-methods study (secondary data analysis and focus groups)
exposure: Preferences for participation in child nutrition research and interventions
Acceptability of workplace recruitment and intervention delivery
outcome: Fathers' preferred type, delivery mode, location, and timing of nutrition interventions
Feasibility of recruiting fathers through workplaces
Acceptability of delivering interventions through workplaces
cohort: Study 1: 463 fathers of preschool children; Study 2: 28 fathers (focus groups and interviews)
finding: Fathers are actively engaged in child feeding and are interested in nutrition information, preferring family-focused interventions delivered online, but show mixed opinions on workplace-based interventions.
